collection_summary: Factual-lookup instance recording the EU accession year for each of the 27 current EU member states, grounded in the Wikipedia 'Member state of the European Union' member-states table. Universe is the 27 current members (the United Kingdom is excluded as a former member, withdrawn 2020). 'Year of EU Accession' is the year of the accession date the table lists for each state: the six founding members are dated to the Treaty of Rome (1957) and later entrants to their enlargement effective dates. Claim type is `source_defined` because the natural-language question 'in what year did each member join' has multiple defensible conventions for the founders (1957 Treaty signed vs. 1958 Treaty in force vs. 1993 Maastricht / EU per se); this instance commits to the convention used by the cited Wikipedia member-state table (all six founders = 1957). Result: 27 rows × 2 columns, sorted by accession year then country.
source_coverage_notes: Single-source instance grounded in the Wikipedia 'Member state of the European Union' table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_state_of_the_European_Union). That table defines both the universe (the 27 current member states; it lists the UK separately as a former member) and the accession year per state (the 'Acceded' column). The 27-row count and the enlargement waves match the standard sequence: 6 founders at 1957 (Treaty of Rome, shown as 'Founder'), then 1973 (Denmark, Ireland), 1981 (Greece), 1986 (Portugal, Spain), 1995 (Austria, Finland, Sweden), 2004 (Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia), 2007 (Bulgaria, Romania), 2013 (Croatia). Construction history: the instance was originally built from the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint (P463=Q458, P580 start-time, excluding P582); it was re-grounded to the Wikipedia member-state table during repair because the raw P580 values dated Germany to 1958 while the other five founders were 1957.
decision_log: 1) Chose query_category=factual_lookup because the query is point-recall per entity — for each known member, a single attribute (year) is looked up. The category's stress is pure parametric recall, not decomposition or scope reasoning, which is exactly what this instance tests. 2) Chose operation_type='projection' to match the curation UI validator's accepted pairing (factual_lookup → projection). The query shape — universe given, single attribute returned per row — is a multi-row projection of one attribute. The membership-status filter is part of universe definition, not the dominant operation. (An earlier draft used 'filter' here; corrected after audit feedback that the validator rejects factual_lookup → filter.) 3) [Construction history] Originally used the statement-node SPARQL form (p:P463/ps:P463 + pq:P580 + pq:P582) rather than the truthy shortcut `wdt:P463`, because reading qualifiers requires the full statement node. 4) [Construction history] Used the safer SPARQL pattern from `references/sparql-gotchas.md` §1 Option B by explicitly excluding deprecated-rank statements. 5) Excluded the UK; in the original SPARQL build via `FILTER NOT EXISTS pq:P582` (UK P463=Q458 carries P582=2020-01-31 Brexit), and in the current Wikipedia-grounded build because the member-state table lists the UK as a former member, not among the 27 current rows. 6) [SUPERSEDED by item 8] The original build did NOT manually unify the founders' accession year: Wikidata recorded France, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, and Netherlands at 1957 (Treaty signed) and Germany at 1958 (Treaty in force), and unifying from Wikidata alone was judged to be parametric-knowledge generation under the curation hard rules. 7) Set claim_type='source_defined' rather than 'exhaustive' because the natural-language question allows multiple defensible date conventions per founder; the instance commits to one source's convention rather than asserting an objectively unique year. 8) REPAIR (cycle 2, addresses the Codex audit cycle 1 BLOCKING finding): re-grounded the instance from the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint to the Wikipedia 'Member state of the European Union' table and normalized Germany's accession year 1958 → 1957 so all six founders are consistently 1957. This reverses item 6: that decision declined to unify the founders because doing so from Wikidata alone would have been parametric, but the Wikipedia member-state table is a direct authoritative source that itself dates all six founders to the Treaty of Rome (25 March 1957, labelled 'Founder'), so the unified 1957 value is now source-grounded, not parametric. gt_construction was therefore changed sparql_wikidata → manual_wikipedia, source_urls re-pointed to the member-state article, and source_count kept at 1. The .sparql file is retained as build history but is no longer authoritative (re-running it would re-introduce DE=1958). claim_type remains source_defined: the founders' year is still the cited table's chosen convention (Treaty-of-Rome signing year), so the instance commits to the source's convention rather than asserting a uniquely correct year.
normalization_decisions: Country names use the canonical English form as in the cited Wikipedia member-state table ('Czech Republic', 'Germany'). 'Year of EU Accession' is a bare integer year (e.g., 2013) per protocol §6; it is the year of the accession date the cited table lists. The six founding members are unified to 1957 (Treaty of Rome, the year the cited table assigns to all six 'Founder' rows); Germany's earlier 1958 value (from raw Wikidata P580 = Treaty in force) was normalized to 1957 to match the source and remove the founder-cohort inconsistency. Sort order is (accession year ASC, country ASC), so the unified 1957 founders now sort as Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands. Single-column primary key on Country is sufficient because each current member has exactly one accession.
open_questions: 1) RESOLVED (repair cycle 2): the founders' accession-year split (Germany 1958 vs. the other five 1957) is fixed — all six founders are now 1957, grounded in the Wikipedia 'Member state of the European Union' table, which dates all six 'Founder' rows to the Treaty of Rome (25 March 1957). The instance now commits to that single convention; an LLM under test that answers 1958 or 1993 for a founder scores as incorrect against the source convention, which the `source_defined` claim type discloses. 2) Whether to count membership in EU predecessor organizations (ECSC 1951, EEC 1957/58) as 'joining the EU' is a definitional choice; the cited table treats the Treaty of Rome (EEC) as the founders' accession event, which this instance follows. 3) The benchmark target for factual_lookup is 3 instances; this is the first. Future siblings could test other crisp date-recall facts (e.g., NATO accession years, ASEAN accession years) without conceptual overlap. 4) If a future EU expansion or contraction occurs (Albania, Moldova, Ukraine acceding, or another departure), this instance's row count will change; the temporal_note records the access date so the snapshot is unambiguous. 5) The artifact-contract operation-type vocabulary table does not currently list factual_lookup → projection as an expected pairing, though the UI validator accepts it; a future artifact-contract update should add that row to prevent the next labeler from guessing wrong.
